Method of Attack: Backdoor allowing remote connection to Linux shell for full device access
Does not open ports and bypasses firewalls
Uses Berkeley Packet Filter (BPF) sniffer to monitor network traffic at low level
Parses ICMP, UDP, and TCP packets for magic data and password to execute commands
Monitors any port including those used by legitimate services
Modifies iptables rules to redirect attacker traffic through firewall
Masquerades binary as common Linux system daemons
Uses anti-forensics techniques including wiping process environment and timestomping
Spawns new instances and changes firewall rules upon receiving special packets
Attack Vector: Network packets with specific magic data and password
Remote commands sent via specially crafted network packets
Indicators of Compromise: Modified iptables rules redirecting attacker traffic
Hardcoded command strings: justtryit, justrobot, justforfun, socket, sockettcp

Masqueraded process names: /sbin/udevd -d, /sbin/mingetty /dev/tty7, /usr/sbin/console-kit-daemon --no-daemon, hald-addon-acpi, dbus-daemon --system, hald-runner, pickup -l -t fifo -u, avahi-daemon, /sbin/auditd -n, /usr/lib/systemd/systemd-journald
Presence of at least 21 versions detected on VirusTotal since August 2018
Publicly available source code on Pastebin (older 2018 version)
